chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the matter that a seeker seeks from his Lord, he said: 'Give charity during your day to sixty poor people; upon each poor person is one Sa' (measure), by the Sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So when he and his family). So when it is night, you bathe in the remaining third (of the night) and wear the least that one who has dependents wears from clothes, except that upon you, from those clothes, should be an izar (loincloth).

Then you pray two Rak'at. So when you place your forehead in the final Rak'at for prostration, you extol Allah, magnify Him, glorify Him, and sanctify Him, and mention your sins, and acknowledge with what you recognize from them specifically, then you raise your head.

Then when you place your head for the second prostration, you seek the choice of Allah one hundred times: 'O Allah, I seek Your choice.' Then you supplicate to Allah with whatever you wish, and ask Him of it; and every time you prostrate, expose your knees to the ground, then raise the loincloth so that you expose them, and place the loincloth behind you between your buttocks and the inner part of your shins.

key_terms.إِزَاراً: A loincloth or lower garment, specified here as a required item of clothing for the ritual.
key_terms.اسْتَخَرْتَ: To seek the best choice or divine preference from God.
key_terms.السُّجُودِ: Prostration, a key component of the prayer ritual described.
key_terms.رُكْبَتَيْكَ: The two knees, which are to be exposed to the ground during prostration in this specific ritual.
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A traditional unit of volume/measurement for charity, specifically the Sa' of the Prophet.

ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step ritual for performing the prayer to fulfill a specific need in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the ritual of Salat al-Hajah, emphasizing the integration of material charity (sadaqah to sixty poor) with spiritual devotion to prepare the heart for supplication. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on specific physical postures, such as uncovering the knees during prostration, as acts of humility that facilitate the acceptance of one's requests from Allah.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Abu Dawood, from Al-Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Zurara,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding the matter sought by the seeker, from his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, said: ‘Give charity during your day upon sixty poor ones, upon each poor one being one Sa’a (approx. 3kg.) of the Sa’a of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So when it is the night-time, what during the remaining third (of the night) and wear the least one can wear from the clothes except that upon you, from those clothes, should be a loin cloth.

Then you should pray two Rak’at of Salāt. So when you place your forehead during the last Rak’at for the Sajdah, you should Extol Allahazwj, and Hisazwj Magnificence, and Hisazwj Holiness, and Hisazwj Glory, and mention your sins, and acknowledge with what you recognise from these, specifically, then raise your head.

When you place your head for the second Sajdah, seek the Choice of Allahazwj one hundred times, ‘O Allahazwj! I seek Yoursaww Choice’. Then supplicate to Allahazwj with whatever you so desire to, and ask Himazwj of it; and every time you perform Sajdah, so expose your knees to touch the ground, and secure the loincloth from behind between his legs’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and abu Dawud from al-Husayn ibn SaTd from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

one who wishes that his Lord make his wish come true should feed sixty destitute people as an act of charity, one sa‘ (three kilograms), by the sa‘ of the Holy Prophet, of food per person. At night during the last third of the night, take a shower and dress in minimum form, except that it must have a loincloth.

Then he should perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer). When placing his forehead on the ground in the last sajdah of the last Rak‘at, he should say that no one, other than Allah, deserves worship, speak of His greatness, His Holiness, His glory and then remember his sins and confess, as much as he remembers, name them (one by one), committing them then raise his head.

When he places his forehead on the ground for the second sajdah, he should ask Allah, one hundred times, to choose for him the best, saying, ‘O Allah, I ask You to choose for me the best.’ Then pray to Allah for whatever he wants. Whenever in sajdah he should expose his knees to touch the ground and secure the loincloth from behind between his legs.”
